key_insight: Attack-policy selection can substantially change measured monitor evasion rates, making basic evaluations falsely reassuring.
engineering_relevance: Monitor evaluations should vary attack-generation methods and optimisation levels, and justify why simulated attacks represent deployment risks.
method: Evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor using attack-generated transcripts.
Develop attacks against proxy monitors and test transfer to a held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor.
Compare attack-generation methods and optimisation levels.
evidence_signal: Measured false negative rates ranged from 0.5% to 20.8% across reinforcement-learning optimisation levels and from 6.4% to 23.0% across methods at their best observed optimisation levels.
watch_item: Attack transcripts may contain artefacts that influence monitor judgments, so transfer success alone does not establish deployment relevance or conservativeness.
paper_title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
